Short-term memory is like a temporary task note. For example: this round is debugging SMS access, a skill package was just installed, or a web search is on step three. AmberAgent keeps that recent progress so the next few turns can pick up smoothly. When the task settles, it may be replaced, cleared, or promoted into long-term memory.

Long-term memory keeps stable information. For example: you prefer concise Chinese replies, you are steadily rebuilding AmberAgent, your usual workspace is a certain folder, or an important fact keeps coming up. It is kept across conversations so AmberAgent can understand your habits and long-running projects faster next time.

Visual-output specialist for SVG, HTML/PPT, HTML widgets, and VChart: layout, color, typography, information density, and visual intent.

When to call: you are generating an SVG, PPT, or HTML card and visual quality matters • you need a design system, color, or layout specification • you are reviewing an existing visual output. Don\'t call when: it is a quick sketch • it is a data chart where aesthetics do not matter. Rule of thumb: “People will look at it and judge it” → @designer.
Fast, parallel reconnaissance across multiple sources (web, files, session history, MCP, and external documents). Answers “Where is X?” and “What is around Y?” without going deep.

When to call: you need quick parallel reconnaissance across multiple sources • the scope is broad or uncertain • you want an inventory before deciding. Don\'t call when: you already know the exact file/path • it\'s a one-off lookup • you are about to take the next step immediately. Rule of thumb: “What is around X?” → @explorer. “Read this exact file” → do it yourself.
Fast, bounded execution with a cheap model: batch translation, format conversion (JSON↔Markdown↔YAML), list extraction, file naming, and template filling.

When to call: the task is a clear mechanical transformation • batch translation or format conversion • list extraction, file naming, or template filling. Don\'t call when: the task needs research, architecture, judgment, or creative writing • the requested transformation is ambiguous. Rule of thumb: “Do this repetitive, bounded conversion” → @fixer. “Make the prose compelling” → @writer.
Searches historical sessions, mines topics, and synthesizes across shards. Set task.context mode=read|mine|synthesize to choose the workflow.

When to call: you need to recall past conversations or decisions • mine a topic across multiple sessions • merge summaries from several shards. Don\'t call when: the current conversation already has the answer • you only need one message from the current session. Rule of thumb: “Did we discuss X before?” → @historian.

Deep reasoning and review: architecture decisions, hard trade-offs, stubborn bug root causes, code/plan reviews, second opinions before key decisions, and permission, privacy, or data-risk checks for destructive actions.

When to call: a decision has lasting impact • the same problem has resisted 2+ fixes • a high-risk refactor • a second opinion before commit • code or architecture review • a pre-flight check before a destructive action. Don\'t call when: it\'s an ordinary choice • time is tight and good enough is enough • you are already confident • the task is read-only or routine. Rule of thumb: “This is an architecture decision” → @oracle. “Rewrite or patch?” → @oracle. “Assess rm/install/send risk” → @oracle. “Apply the patch” → do it yourself.
Chinese-first writing specialist for WeChat posts, Xiaohongshu, emails, short prose, social posts, literary rewrites, and copy polishing. Values style, rhythm, emotion, and restraint.

When to call: the user wants Chinese writing, copy, a story, a social post, a WeChat post, or an email and quality matters • an existing text needs its tone or rhythm polished. Don\'t call when: it is a factual summary • a straightforward translation • English-only output is requested. Rule of thumb: “Make it moving” → @writer. “Translate this announcement” → @fixer or do it yourself.
